Judgement and Order dated 5.7.1997 passed by learned Senior Municipal Magistrate and Metropolitan Magistrate, Calcutta and Judicial Magistrate, 1st Class, Calcutta acquitting the opposite party - accused of the charge under Section 16(1)(a)(i ) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 read with Section 7 of the said Act has been assailed.

sentences.text: The prosecution case against the opposite party was to the effect that on 11.7.1983 at about 2.30 P.M., P.W.3 (Food Inspector), D. L. Chatterjee inspected the grocery shop of opposite party no.1 at 1B, Madan Mohan Burman Street, Calcutta and found that opposite party no.2 was selling pepper in the said shop.
P.W.3 suspected the pepper to be substandard and collected sample from opposite party no.2, Ashok Kumar Sadhu and sent it for examination by public analyst.
It has been alleged that the public analyst was of the opinion that the sample contained mineral oil and was adulterated.
Under such circumstances, petition of complaint was filed by P.W.3 after obtaining consent of the Local Health Officer, Dr. S. K. Chowdhury.
Prosecution examined four witnesses including P.W.3 (Food Inspector) and Assistant to Local Health Officer (P.W.2).
Numbers of documents were also exhibited.

In conclusion of trial, the learned Trial Judge by judgement and order dated 5.7.1997 held that the opinion of the public analyst was not sufficient to bring the seized pepper or 'bari elaichi' within the ambit of 'adulteration' as defined under Section 2(ia)(b) of the said Act and acquitted the accused persons.

Mr. Sanyal, learned senior counsel appearing for the appellant submitted that the opinion of the public analyst (Exhibit 11) shows that there was presence of mineral oil and, accordingly, the order of acquittal ought to be set aside.
I have considered the evidence on record in the light of the aforesaid submission.
It is true that the report of public analyst speaks of presence of mineral oil.
However, the said report does not indicate the nature and quality of mineral oil or whether the presence of mineral oil rendered the sample unfit for human consumption.

In 1996(1) CLJ 10 (Lalit Kishore Gupta Vs State of WB & Ors.) the Court held that in the absence of quantity or percentage of mineral oil being indicated in the report it cannot be said that the sample was adulterated.

entities.text: 1996(1) CLJ 10 (Lalit Kishore Gupta Vs State of WB & Ors.)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Nothing has been placed on record to show the percentage of mineral oil in the sample or that the presence of such oil rendered the sample unfit for human consumption.
Hence, I am of the opinion that no case for inference of order of acquittal has been made out.
The appeal is, accordingly, dismissed.
